div.h2: A journey from Dhaka's streets to the fine-dining table.
div.p: Chef Zafar Ahmed is a chef, mentor, entrepreneur, and consultant building a more ambitious culinary future for Bangladesh.
I grew up in the busy streets of Dhaka, surrounded by noise, narrow alleys, and the smell of colourful street food. From childhood, I felt a strong pull toward cooking.
My culinary journey began in 2009. Slowly, I earned my place in the kitchens of four top five-star hotels in Dhaka: The Westin, Le Méridien, Renaissance and InterContinental.
That experience introduced me to fine dining. I learned that food is more than something to eat — it is an experience, and every plate tells a story.
I shared kitchens with master chefs from France, Greece, Germany, China, Malaysia, Indonesia and Italy when they came to Bangladesh, and became especially skilled in Mediterranean cuisine.
My cooking has reached the Honorable President of Bangladesh, Nobel Laureate Dr. Muhammad Yunus, cricket stars and many more — but the best reward is a regular guest saying, "Wow, that was amazing!"
I discovered molecular gastronomy, which combines science and art to change the texture, smell and look of food. I want to be part of its future in Bangladesh.
I started AromaVilla Cooking School to give young people the tools to build a better future — to dream, and to turn those dreams into reality.
I am a teacher, entrepreneur, mentor and consultant. My goal is to bring Bangladesh's culinary world to the global stage.

div.blockquote:
"Food is not just fuel for the body — it's a language of love, stories, and discovery."
— Chef Zafar Ahmed
